record: TWO ENFORCED RELEASE CONDITIONS, AND THE VALIDATION THAT CAN SEE THEM
supersedes_nothing: PRODUCTION_READBACK_2026-09-27.json still stands; this is the bounded work that followed it

the_defect: checked the AGE OF THE ASSESSMENT. Selection therefore restarted both clocks:
a book observed 29 s ago under a 30 s bound bought a further 30 s by being
looked at, and an order could leave against an observation 59 s old with every
field in the trace reading 'within bound'. What expires is the OBSERVATION.

the_rule_now.deadline: min(book stamp + book bound, probability stamp + the bound its event state permits)

checked_twice: before anything is written, so an already-expired assessment reserves nothing
again at the last instant before the send, AFTER _reserve_exit's SELECT ... FOR UPDATE -- the wait that can consume what is left of it

an_expired_reservation_is_released.how: FB.abandon_proven_not_sent, the same path the venue-boundary denial uses
an_expired_reservation_is_released.consequence: the exit row is ABANDONED, which bettor_funded_available_to_exit does not count, so the inventory returns for the re-assessment that should replace it
an_expired_reservation_is_released.counted_on_the_answer: submit_exit returns venue_calls, so 'nothing was sent' is a readback rather than a reassurance

1_the_inputs_own_remaining_lifetime.no_deadline_at_all: refused with NO_INPUT_EXPIRY_WAS_CARRIED_TO_THIS_SUBMISSION on the path that could reach the venue

counterexamples_each_failing_before_and_.case: book already 29 s old; submit two seconds later
counterexamples_each_failing_before_and_.asserts: remaining_lifetime_s < 2 at selection, governed_by VENUE_BOOK, then refusal at +2 s with venue_calls 0 and no create call
governed_by PROBABILITY, probability_expires_at < book_expires_at, and the carried deadline equals the probability's

counterexamples_each_failing_before_and_.case: reservation lock delays submission beyond the deadline
counterexamples_each_failing_before_and_.how: a second connection genuinely holds SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the position and releases it after the deadline passes
counterexamples_each_failing_before_and_.asserts: venue_calls 0, no create call, reservation taken AND released, available_to_exit back to 10.0, the exit row ABANDONED and not outstanding

and_the_automated_path_is_what_is_tested.why: manage() must pass the selector's deadline into submit_exit; had it dropped it, the submission would refuse rather than send on an unbounded assessment

1_the_inputs_own_remaining_lifetime.retired: MAX_ASSESSMENT_AGE_S -- the constant that granted the window

the_state_it_covers: start.sh serves after a failed migration on purpose: the diagnostics are how
the failure gets found. On 2026-09-27 that left the API running with funded
code naming columns the database did not have. Availability was right and
CAPABILITY was not -- nothing stopped the funded lane.

required.migrations: REPORTED, NOT ENFORCED -- schema_migrations records what the runner believes; the objects are what queries run against, and the two legitimately differ (the gate applies files with psql and records nothing). Production had both missing, so it would still have blocked

what_reports_instead_of_raising: bettor_funded_management.manage -> funded_capability BLOCKED, nothing reconciled settled or sent
bettor_funded_book.command_center -> BLOCKED with the missing objects named, and the counts WITHHELD rather than shown as zeros
2_schema_readiness_is_an_enforced_condit.what_stays_available: every non-funded route, the diagnostics, and the desk read itself

the_production_failure_state_is_tested.how: the tests drop `residual_qty` and the ledger rows inside a transaction that is rolled back, so the broken state is real and temporary
the_production_failure_state_is_tested.the_second_one_flips_every_switch_ON: FUNDED_SUBMISSION_ENABLED, FUNDED_EXIT_SUBMISSION_ENABLED and REAL_ORDER_SUBMISSION_ENABLED are all monkeypatched true, so the schema condition ALONE is what stops the venue being reached: zero create, preview or cancel calls
the_production_failure_state_is_tested.and_a_ledger_gap_alone_does_not_block: asserted in the first test -- deleting the 126 row while every object is present reads AVAILABLE

2_schema_readiness_is_an_enforced_condit.start_sh: unchanged in behaviour and now states the consequence where an operator reads it

why: the release gate's database is PostgreSQL 16.13 and production is 18.6. A green
gate on the wrong major version established nothing about migration 126, and
saying so afterwards is not the same as testing it.
what_it_does: postgres:18 service container, asserts server_version_num >= 170000 or fails
applies every migration with `python -m sportsassets.scripts.migrate` -- the runner production boots with, asyncpg, whole file per transaction
a funded file that fails FAILS THE JOB; two pre-existing files that depend on a collector-built table are skipped by name and reported
asserts 125, 126, 127 and 128 recorded, the new columns present, the predicates present

asserts bettor_funded_one_open_position BUILT, evaluates the predicate under search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, and REINDEXes the index -- the real maintenance operation, which 17+ runs under that path itself
runs the five funded test files against that database
3_the_migrations_are_exercised_on_postgr.what_it_still_does_not_do: run the WHOLE suite on 18. It covers the funded lane's migrations and tests, which is where the defect was

4_operator_access_is_proven_not_merely_r.the_gap: a wrong-password probe returning 401 establishes that the sign-in REJECTS. It says nothing about whether anybody can get in
4_operator_access_is_proven_not_merely_r.credentials: read from the service environment through the Render API, masked before use, never printed, never rotated, never typed as a workflow input

results_against_the_serving_build.POST /api/command/session/control (corre: HTTP 200, scope control, cookie set, token_in_body false, ttl 1800 s
results_against_the_serving_build.GET /api/command/bettor/desk with the se: HTTP 200, 15 sections, no admin token on the request
results_against_the_serving_build.GET a read route with the CONTROL cookie: HTTP 401 -- asserted as the correct scope boundary: the control credential does not grant reads

a_finding_that_is_an_owner_decision: DESK_PASSWORD is NOT SET on the service. That does not close the read sign-in:
config.Settings.desk_password carries a default and /api/command/session accepts
it, so the command centre's READ surface is currently protected by a value
published in this repository. The step signs in with it -- read out of the
checked-out source, never retyped, never printed -- to prove desk access
genuinely works, and reports the situation rather than hiding it or calling the
sign-in unconfigured. The CONTROL credential, which the write actions need, is a
two_defects_in_this_step_itself_found_an: it read the CONTROL cookie against a READ route, got 401, and narrated that as 'confirms the session is live'. It confirms the opposite, and the opposite is correct
it reported 'not configured' when DESK_PASSWORD was absent, which would have been misleading in the other direction

5_what_the_gate_actually_said.note: filled in after the final pair; the intermediate pair is kept because discarding an inconvenient reading is how an instrument stops being one

what_this_record_does_not_claim: that funded readiness is complete. It is not: no account is bound, no credential is provisioned, no limits are approved, and section 3 of the handoff lists the market evidence that is still missing.
that these tests establish anything about a venue, a source or a fixture. They are software conditions.
that the PostgreSQL 18 job makes the 16 gate redundant. It covers the funded lane only.
